name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis, including an in-driver taste-funnel explore state and design-ratification state) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (spec-build-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, and the ledger row driven; test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, and repair held by the session) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.50.0 — unified build loop (specs/20260901/03-unified-build-loop.md): /spec:build becomes the per-feature loop carrying a spec from hardened to done, deriving the next stage from disk and running design (when due), then the build driver, then the review driver in sequence, each `--via loop`. One checkpoint is enforced: a loop-driven review parks at a new CHECKPOINT state after the reviewer returns and refuses DISPOSITIONS until the session id in `.claude/spec-session.json` changes (a `/clear` and re-run), once per run, degrading to a printed warning when no stamp exists; the pre-merge stop stays the existing worktree step-out, never a forced clear. `spec-state-gate.sh` admits `/spec:build` on `hardened|implementing|done`. `core.md`'s § State Machine now attributes each transition to a driver state rather than a command: plan's lock → `hardened`, the build driver's preflight → `implementing`, the review driver's close → `done`; `/spec:build` runs both drivers in sequence and `/spec:review` remains the review driver's direct entry. `fleet-reader.js` gains the seventh fixed question `cleanByVia`, scoring escapes-per-CLEAN separately for `loop` / `direct` / `unknown` review rows — the number the brief's kill condition reads. 7.49.0 — run provenance (specs/20260901/02-run-provenance.md): brief 18's kill condition needs every review and build row to say which command shape produced it (`via: loop|direct`) and which model held the session, and neither existed — the session model is not in the shell environment and no row carried it. A never-blocking `UserPromptSubmit` hook, `spec-session-stamp.sh`, now stamps `session_id`/`transcript_path`/`cwd`/`ts` to a per-root, gitignored `.claude/spec-session.json` on every `/spec:` prompt (any other prompt or failure exits 0, writes nothing); `lib/session-stamp.js` derives `sessionModel(root)` from the last assistant line of that transcript's tail, failing soft to `null` on any format surprise. `verdict.js` gains `--via loop|direct` (default `direct`, refused with `--profile release`) and `--model <id>`, writing both onto the review row right after `tier`; both drivers accept `--via`, record it once in their sidecar at creation, and pass it plus the derived model onto every row they write. `init-gen.js`'s `IGNORE_ENTRIES` and this repo's `.gitignore` both gain the stamp path so it never rides a close commit. 7.48.0 — build driver (specs/20260901/01-build-driver.md): /spec:build was the last per-feature stage whose deterministic choreography — admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, env preflight, the status flip, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, diff counts, the hand-written ledger row — was still performed by an LLM. spec-build-driver.js (spec-paths build-driver) now re-derives the build's state from spec frontmatter + a `<spec>.build/` sidecar + on-disk artifacts on every invocation, executes every one of those steps itself, and prints exactly one judgment step at a time (test-author dispatch, red attribution, per-wave worker dispatch, host integration, repair dispatch, the checkpoint commit) behind a closed, artifact-verified mark set; a fourth `repair-applied` parks the run at the terminal ESCALATE state instead of looping past the 3-round cap. build.md shrinks to the judgment shell mirroring review.md's shape. Build ledger rows are now script-written and carry `runId` (`bd_`), `redCheck`, and `workers: {spawned, continued}` alongside the original four fields. `lib/driver-io.js` extracts the four helpers both drivers need (`runChild`, `writeOut`, `appendLedger`, sidecar load/save) out of spec-review-driver.js, behavior byte-identical.
